met_analysis:
The Well Marked Low Pressure Area (Remnant of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”) over central parts of Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha now lies over north Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood at 0530 hrs IST of 30th October, 2026. It is very likely to continue to move north-northeastwards, and weaken further into a low pressure area over Northeast Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood during next 24 hours.
The Low Pressure Area over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood persisted over the same region at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 30th October 2026. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and concentrate into a depression over southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea around 31st October. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and continue to move west-northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan and neighbourhood between 3.1 and 4.5 km above mean sea level with the trough aloft in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 20°N.
The Induced upper air cyclonic circulation over south Punjab & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over West Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough from the cyclonic circulation associated with the Well marked low pressure area over central parts of Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha to the cyclonic circulation over south Konkan across Telangana and North Interior Karnataka extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan and neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
